conditional: A federal statutory or regulatory delay of the 2025 reconciliation law's Medicaid community-engagement compliance deadline is announced on or before 2027-03-31, pushing the effective date beyond April 2027.

findings.summary: The final resolver is the public SSA-SA-MOWL Field I monthly series, but the forecast rules it out because the run could not stream rows and instead uses annual DI claims received as a proxy.
findings.actionRequested: Use the exact historical SSA-SA-MOWL Field I monthly receipts series, or document a concrete data-access failure and provide a defensible fallback that maps DI/SSI workload totals to Field I receipts.

findings.summary: The stated base rate uses DI annual claims only, while Field I Receipts (All Initial) is a DDS workload measure and may include a different mix than DI claims received alone.
findings.actionRequested: State a base-rate prior from historical Field I April or recent monthly Field I receipts; if retaining the proxy, explain the coverage gap and why SSI/other DDS receipts are not included in the level.

findings.summary: The interval is based on three annual DI proxy values plus judgmental widening, not realized monthly Field I volatility or a clearly calibrated forecast-error distribution.
findings.actionRequested: Calibrate the 80% interval using realized month-to-month, April-specific, or forecast-horizon residual volatility from the SSA-SA-MOWL Field I history; keep any extra policy uncertainty as an explicit additive component.

findings.summary: The +10 thousand trend adjustment to 2027 is only loosely justified from FY2022-FY2024 annual DI growth and not checked against more recent monthly Field I behavior.
findings.actionRequested: Tie the trend update to exact recent Field I observations, or reduce/relabel it as judgmental and explain why annual DI momentum should carry into April 2027 DDS initial receipts.

findings.summary: The reasoning references the opposite no-delay run as a public prior run; this is not outcome leakage, but it risks making the forecast look anchored to another catalog forecast rather than independent evidence.
findings.actionRequested: Keep the comparison only as a consistency check, and make clear the point estimate is derived from source data and stated adjustments, not from the prior catalog/no-delay forecast.

findings.summary: Clarify whether the cited timing file URL should be SSA_DATES1.csv rather than ssa-dates1.htm.
State that 2027-05-30 is a by-date for availability and that the operative resolution is the first file version containing 2027-04, in case SSA posts earlier.
Make the tail cases quantify what combination of trend, month timing, and policy spillover would push the print below 193.4 or above 261.4.

dispositions.rationale: Review disposition: accepted the critiques to downgrade and label the annual DI workload proxy, clarify the Field I coverage gap, avoid anchoring on the no-delay catalog forecast, use SSA_DATES1.csv for the timing source, and widen the interval for proxy and April-seasonality uncertainty. Rejected rebuilding from exact SSA-SA-MOWL monthly Field I history because those rows were not available in the draft evidence; the fallback remains explicit rather than silently inventing monthly target-series history.
